story: At 5:17 on a sunny Thursday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Rosa are chatting in the Town Square about cornbread for Friday dinner and whether her kitchen needs any fixing beforehand. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna and Hal are trading friendly jabs about the pink flamingos in her yard, with Hal insisting she trim the flock to the three allowed by the deed restrictions. Donna has invited him to watch Gary's first pickleball practice at the courts tomorrow at ten, and the whole neighborhood seems to be looking forward to the weekend.

gary.thought_process: Rosa just walked into the Square. Donna already has the courts booked for tomorrow at ten, so that's settled and I don't need to ask again. I'm looking forward to Friday dinner at Rosa's, so the neighborly thing is to say hello and offer to bring the cornbread. I'm helpful to a fault, so I'll ask if she needs anything fixed or carried before Friday. Keep it short and natural.

parameters.content: Evening, Rosa! I'll have cornbread for Friday, and if your table or anything in the kitchen needs fixing beforehand, just say the word. Toolbox is always ready.

donna.thought_process: Hal's right here on Magnolia Loop, and he's already heard about Friday dinner from Rosa. I've booked the courts for ten tomorrow and Gary has his paddle, so the practice is handled. Hal's flamingo jab deserves a comeback, and I'd like to confirm he's bringing his appetite and maybe get him to come watch Gary's first practice. Nobody's pending on a question from me right now, so I'm not repeating myself. A little teasing keeps me at the center of the circle.

parameters.content: I heard that, Hal Weems. The flamingos are staying outside where they belong, but you're welcome to come cheer at the courts tomorrow at ten. Gary's first practice, and I'd like a witness.

hal.thought_process: Donna's right here by her flamingo flock, and I've got a list of grievances I've been sitting on. But Friday dinner at Rosa's is tomorrow, and I'd like to keep the peace. Gary's cart form is the bigger matter and Donna just booked the courts for him, so no sense nagging her about that. Still, flamingo count is flamingo count, and L-02 says three. I'll raise it straight but with a little dry humor, and see what she says. If it's over three, I'll give her a fair chance to fix it before anything goes to the committee.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna. Quick count of that flock for you: the deed restrictions say three visible from the street, and I'm seeing more than three. Trim it down before Friday and I'll leave the clipboard in the drawer.

rosa.thought_process: Gary just arrived at Town Square and I'm here too. Friday dinner is mostly set: Hal and Donna said yes, and Gary's bringing cornbread. Donna's booked the courts for him tomorrow at ten, so the two of them are already bonding, which is exactly what I want. The one thing I haven't done is confirm with Gary face to face about timing and whether he needs anything, and he's standing right here. Keep it short, warm, and forward-moving, not a repeat of the invite.

parameters.content: Gary, good timing. Dinner's Friday at six at my place, so Donna's got you on the courts at ten and you're still home to bake that cornbread. Anything you need from my kitchen, just say so.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
